**Jupiter** is the fifth [planet](/wiki/Planet "Planet") from the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"), and the [largest in the Solar System](/wiki/List_of_Solar_System_objects_by_size "List of Solar System objects by size"). It is a [gas giant](/wiki/Gas_giant "Gas giant") with a [mass](/wiki/Jupiter_mass "Jupiter mass") nearly 2.5 times that of all the other planets in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") combined and slightly less than one-thousandth the mass of the Sun. Its diameter is 11 times that of [Earth](/wiki/Earth "Earth") and a tenth that of the Sun. Jupiter orbits the Sun at a distance of 5.20 [AU](/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit") (778.5 [Gm](/wiki/Gigametre "Gigametre")), with an [orbital period](/wiki/Orbital_period "Orbital period") of 11.86 [years](/wiki/Julian_year_(astronomy) "Julian year (astronomy)"). It is the [third-brightest natural object](/wiki/List_of_brightest_natural_objects_in_the_sky "List of brightest natural objects in the sky") in the Earth's [night sky](/wiki/Night_sky "Night sky"), after the [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon") and [Venus](/wiki/Venus "Venus"), and has been observed since [prehistoric times](/wiki/Prehistoric_times "Prehistoric times"). Its name derives from that of [Jupiter](/wiki/Jupiter_(god) "Jupiter (god)"), the chief deity of [ancient Roman religion](/wiki/Ancient_Roman_religion "Ancient Roman religion").

Jupiter was the first of the Sun's planets to form, and its inward migration during the primordial phase of the Solar System affected much of the formation history of the other planets. Ed Rendell :: Early life :: chunk_0002
Ed Rendell was born on January 5, 1944, in New York City, the son of Emma (*née* Sloat) and Jesse T. Rendell. His parents were [Jewish](/wiki/Jew "Jew"), and all four of his grandparents were immigrants from Russia.[[4]](#cite_note-Rendell_Ancestry-4) He attended [Riverdale Country School](/wiki/Riverdale_Country_School "Riverdale Country School") before the [University of Pennsylvania](/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), where he joined the [Pi Lambda Phi](/wiki/Pi_Lambda_Phi "Pi Lambda Phi") fraternity[[5]](#cite_note-5) in 1962 and earned a [B.A.](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in 1965. In 1968, he earned a [J.D.](/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") at [Villanova University School of Law](/wiki/Villanova_University_School_of_Law "Villanova University School of Law"). He served as a [2nd Lieutenant](/wiki/2nd_Lieutenant "2nd Lieutenant") in the [U.S. Army Reserve](/wiki/U.S._Army_Reserve "U.S. Army Reserve") from 1968 to 1974.

fanoutqa_039206.x:
Xiluodu Dam :: Design :: chunk_0003
The Xiluodu is a 285.5 m (937 ft) tall and 700 m (2,300 ft) long double-curvature arch dam. It is the third tallest arch dam in the world and a key component of the [Jinsha River](/wiki/Jinsha_River "Jinsha River") Project. It withholds a reservoir of 12,670,000,000 cubic metres (10,270,000 [acre⋅ft](/wiki/Acre-foot "Acre-foot")) of which 6,460,000,000 cubic metres (5,240,000 [acre⋅ft](/wiki/Acre-foot "Acre-foot")) is considered active storage for power generation. The dam contains several [spillways](/wiki/Spillway "Spillway") to include seven surface outlets, eight mid-level orifices and four spillway tunnels. All spillways afford a maximum discharge of 32,278 m3/s (1,139,900 cu ft/s).[[9]](#cite_note-9) The dam's power station is split into two [underground power stations](/wiki/Underground_power_station "Underground power station"), one located behind the right abutment, the second behind the left abutment. Each power station contains nine 770 MW [Francis turbine](/wiki/Francis_turbine "Francis turbine")-generators for a total installed capacity of 13,860 MW.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

McNair formerly served as executive at [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") and [Sacramento Kings](/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").

McNair grew up in [Oak Park, California](/wiki/Oak_Park,_California "Oak Park, California"), and attended [Oak Park High School](/wiki/Oak_Park_High_School_(California) "Oak Park High School (California)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

McNair earned a [Bachelor of Science](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [computer science](/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science") from [Princeton University](/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University") in 2006. While attending college, McNair was a wide receiver on the [football team](/wiki/Princeton_Tigers_football "Princeton Tigers football").[[2]](#cite_note-2) From 2006 to 2007, he was a sports programmer and researcher at [STATS LLC](/wiki/Stats_Perform "Stats Perform").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

The population of the City of Paris was 2,102,650 in January 2023, down from 2,165,423 in January 2022, according to the [INSEE](/wiki/Institut_national_de_la_statistique_et_des_%C3%A9tudes_%C3%A9conomiques "Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques"), the French statistical agency. Between 2013 and 2023, the population fell by 122,919, or about five percent. The Mayor of Paris, [Anne Hidalgo](/wiki/Anne_Hidalgo "Anne Hidalgo"), declared that this illustrated the "de-densification" of the city, creating more green space and less crowding.[[153]](#cite_note-155)[[154]](#cite_note-156) Despite the drop, Paris remains the most densely populated city in Europe, with 252 residents per hectare, not counting parks.[[155]](#cite_note-Le_Monde,_22_January_2019-157) This drop was attributed partly to a lower birth rate, the departure of middle-class residents, and the possible loss of housing in Paris, due to short-term rentals for tourism.[[156]](#cite_note-ReferenceA-158)

Paris is the fourth largest municipality in the European Union, after [Berlin](/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), [Madrid](/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") and [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome"), and is the [34th most densely populated city in the world](/wiki/List_of_cities_proper_by_population_density "List of cities proper by population density") as of 2020.[[157]](#cite_note-worldatlas-pop-159) [Eurostat](/wiki/Eurostat "Eurostat") places Paris (6.5 million people) behind London (8 million) and ahead of Berlin (3.5 million), based on the 2012 populations of what Eurostat calls "urban audit core cities".[[158]](#cite_note-160)
The population of Paris today is lower than its historical peak of 2.9 million in 1921.[[159]](#cite_note-161) The principal reasons are a significant decline in household size and a dramatic migration of residents to the suburbs between 1962 and 1975. Bronx Science has received international recognition. In 2020, Newsweek's rankings of the top 5,000 STEM High Schools in the United States (public and private), listed Bronx Science as the 4th best STEM school in the nation.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

In 2014, the school ranked 34th out of all high schools nationwide and 1st in [New York](/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)");[[27]](#cite_note-27) nationwide, Bronx Science ranked 33rd in 2008 and 58th in 2009.[[28]](#cite_note-28) It attracts an intellectually gifted blend of culturally, ethnically,[[29]](#cite_note-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30) and economically diverse students from New York City.[[31]](#cite_note-transport-31) As of 2012, Bronx Science is ranked as one of the "22 top-performing schools"[[32]](#cite_note-32) in America on *[The Washington Post](/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* as well as number 50 out of a list of the best 1,000 high schools in the country on [The Daily Beast](/wiki/Daily_Beast "Daily Beast")'s "America's Best High Schools"[[33]](#cite_note-33) list. In 2014 it was ranked second highest on *Cities Journal*'s list of the "15 Best High Schools in New York",[[34]](#cite_note-CJ_Science-34) along with Stuyvesant (ranked third)[[35]](#cite_note-CJ_Stuy-35) and Brooklyn Tech (ranked eighth).[[36]](#cite_note-CJ_Bk_Tech-36)

The average [SAT](/wiki/SAT "SAT") score at Bronx Science was 2100 out of 2400.[[37]](#cite_note-dailybeast-sat-37) Almost all Bronx Science graduates continue on to four-year colleges, and it known as a "feeder school", with many graduates going on to [Ivy League](/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League") schools and other institutions of higher learning each year.[[38]](#cite_note-GothamsElite-38) Bronx Science has counted 132 finalists in the [Regeneron](/wiki/Regeneron "Regeneron") (formerly Intel) [Science Talent Search](/wiki/Regeneron_Science_Talent_Search "Regeneron Science Talent Search"), the largest

James Vincent, a reporter from The Verge, comments that "It prods and pokes viewers with unsubtle emotional cues, like a reality TV show would. "Now, you should be nervous; now you should feel relieved". The AlphaGo footage slowly captures the moment when Lee Sedol acknowledges the true power of AlphaGo AI. In the first game, he had more experience than his human-programmed AI, so he thought it would be easy to beat the AI. However, the early game dynamics were not what he expected. After losing the first match, he became more nervous and lost confidence. Afterward, he reacted to attacks by saying that he just wanted to win the match, unintentionally displaying his anger, and acting in an unusual way. Also, he spends 12 minutes on one move, while AlphaGo only takes a minute and a half to respond. AlphaGo weighs each alternative equally and consistently. No reaction to Lee's fight. Instead, the game continues as if he was not there.

James also said that "suffice to say that humanity does land at least one blow on the machines, through Lee's so-called "divine move". "More likely, the forces of automation we'll face will be impersonal and incomprehensible. They'll come in the form of star ratings we can't object to, and algorithms we can't fully understand. Hou Yu-ih :: 2024 presidential election :: chunk_0006
Prior to the 2024 presidential election, Hou was considered the favorite for the Kuomintang presidential primary.[[37]](#cite_note-40) He was drafted by the Kuomintang on 17 May 2023 to be its nominee for the presidency.[[38]](#cite_note-41)[[39]](#cite_note-42)

On 15 November 2023, KMT and [Taiwan People's Party](/wiki/Taiwan_People%27s_Party "Taiwan People's Party") leadership announced that they would field a single joint presidential ticket made up of Hou and TPP chairman [Ko Wen-je](/wiki/Ko_Wen-je "Ko Wen-je"). The order was to be determined by opinion polls and publicly announced on 18 November,[[40]](#cite_note-43) but the parties were unable to reach an agreement on that date.[[41]](#cite_note-44) Hou officially registered his candidacy with running mate [Jaw Shaw-kong](/wiki/Jaw_Shaw-kong "Jaw Shaw-kong") on 24 November 2023, ending the possibility of a joint ticket.[[42]](#cite_note-45) Hou conceded the presidential election to [Lai Ching-te](/wiki/Lai_Ching-te "Lai Ching-te") on 13 January 2024.[[43]](#cite_note-46)[[44]](#cite_note-47) Shortly after Hou lost the presidential election, netizens began efforts to [recall](/wiki/Recall_election#Taiwan "Recall election") him from the New Taipei mayoralty.[[45]](#cite_note-48)

Hou's firstborn son Hou Ni-wei died on 15 May 1992, in a [tour bus fire](/wiki/1992_Taoyuan_County_tour_bus_fire "1992 Taoyuan County tour bus fire"),[[46]](#cite_note-49)[[47]](#cite_note-50)[[48]](#cite_note-51) which killed 23 people.[[49]](#cite_note-52) He and his wife Jen Mei-ling raised three daughters: Hou Yu-fan, Hou Ni-chia, and Hou Yu-chia.[[50]](#cite_note-53)[[51]](#cite_note-54)
